notes.common/nonlinear-disordered-media-photon:
# Nonlinear disordered-media photonic computing

Free-space photonic feature extraction that combines **multiple light scattering** in a disordered medium with **material second-order (χ²) nonlinearity**—typically second-harmonic generation (SHG) under random quasi-phase-matching—so nonlinear optical speckles act as internal activation-rich maps, while linear fundamental-harmonic speckles recover optical random projection. [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [χ² LN slab · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

Wang et al. (arXiv:2310.07690v1) implement this with a lithium niobate nanocrystal slab, SLM phase encoding, dual-camera FH/SH readout, and a trained digital linear layer only. [setup · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) Distinct from [structural / configuration-encoded nonlinearity](structural-nonlinearity.md) and from integrated PIC modulator nonlinearities.

notes.common/on-chip-diffractive-optical-neura:
# On-chip diffractive optical neural network

Integrated photonic neural architecture that performs multilayer transforms by slab-waveguide diffraction between neuron-like scatterers or phase regions on chip, rather than only mesh interferometers or microring weight banks. [DONN concept · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

Early on-chip DONNs often freeze weights into fabricated silicon/silica geometry designed offline, limiting reconfigurability and multimodal retasking. [fixed weights · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) TDONN (trainable DONN) adds massive thermally tunable diffractive units and optical-domain in situ training so one chip can be reconfigured across modalities. [TDONN · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [tunable heaters · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

Distinct from free-space SLM/metasurface stacks and from MZI/MRR PIC meshes, though all serve photonic neural computing.

notes.common/optical-metasurface.md:
# Optical metasurface

Subwavelength-structured free-space optical surface that modulates amplitude/phase of an incident field; in photonic AI it can act as a dense diffractive feature extractor or matrix–vector front end. [metasurface chip · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

Peng et al. (2026) implement a fixed **MetaExtractor** (~41M meta-atoms) whose Gaussian-distributed weights approximate RBF similarity kernels and, with free-space diffraction distance, supply attention-like channel aggregation and local–global receptive fields—without post-fabrication optical reconfiguration. [RBF design · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [fixed after fab · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

Distinct from electrically [programmable optical metasurfaces](programmable-optical-metasurface.md) and from bulk [SLMs](spatial-light-modulator.md), though lab demos may use an SLM to synthesize inputs.

notes.common/photonic-neural-network.md:
# Photonic neural network

Hardware neural networks that perform matrix–vector multiplications and related linear transforms with light (pixels/meta-atoms, waveguides, free-space diffraction), optionally adding optical or electronic nonlinear activations. [PNN definition · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

Motivations commonly cited include bandwidth, parallelism, and lower heat than digital routing of binary signals. [optical advantages · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Implementations span photonic integrated circuits, free-space SLMs/diffractive stacks, cavities, and fibres. [hardware platforms · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

# Sharpness-aware training

Training method for physical neural networks that minimizes not only task loss but also **loss sharpness**, seeking flat minima so parameters stay accurate under model–reality mismatch, fabrication variance, and post-deployment perturbations (thermal drift, misalignment) without assuming a particular noise model. [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [loss sharpness ↔ robustness · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

Inspired by sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) in digital ML, but reframes sharpness as **physical-system robustness** rather than only statistical generalization; implemented with a two-step first-order update (adversarial neighborhood step, then descent) compatible with in silico BP and in situ / [physics-aware (PAT)](physics-aware-training.md) loops. [SAM contrast · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [Eq. (3) · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [in silico and in situ · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

Demonstrated on MRR weight banks, MZI meshes, and free-space diffractive NNs (OLED + SLM), including settings without an explicit misalignment model. [three platforms · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [free-space misalignment · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

# Multimodal deep learning using on-chip diffractive optics with in situ training capability

Nature Communications (2024). DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3. [DOI · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

## Problem and idea

Most photonic neuromorphic processors for deep learning handle only a single modality, partly because abundant optical-domain parameter training is lacking. [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) Prior [on-chip diffractive optical neural networks (DONNs)](../common/on-chip-diffractive-optical-neural-network.md) fix neuron geometry after digital-computer design, so fabricated chips are not reconfigurable and struggle with multimodal tasks that need in situ updates. [fixed DONN · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

This paper proposes and fabricates a trainable diffractive optical neural network ([TDONN](../common/on-chip-diffractive-optical-neural-network.md)) on SOI: one input layer, five hidden layers of thermally tunable diffractive units, and one output layer, with customized SGD and an optical drop-out mechanism for [in situ training](../common/physics-aware-training.md) in the optical domain. [TDONN proposal · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [chip design · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

The work sits in [photonic / optical neural networks (ONNs)](../common/photonic-neural-network.md), where light propagation implements computation with high parallelism and energy efficiency as digital microelectronics hit Moore’s-Law limits for large multimodal AI. [Moore / ONNs · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [propagation-as-computation · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) Established integrated routes include MZI meshes, microring WDM arrays, and PCM crossbars—grouped here under [photonic integrated circuits (PIC / MZI / MRR)](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md)—but device footprints often keep matrix sizes small (e.g. ~4×4), forcing repeated O/E conversion. [MZI/MRR limits · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) On-chip DONNs scale connectivity via slab diffraction; this paper’s contribution is making that route trainable and multimodal rather than a static fabricated transform. [DONN background · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [trainable multimodal · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) Relative to bulky free-space diffraction and fibre systems, TDONN is CMOS-foundry integrable (a free-space contrast in the paper’s Discussion, not a metasurface claim). [vs bulky free-space · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

## Key method

- Hardware: 16 intensity modulators (MZI) load features; 80 TiN micro-heaters in five layers act as trainable diffractive neurons; four PD ports give class probabilities after one optical forward pass. [layers · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [80 heaters · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)
- Training: optical-domain SGD on measured outputs (black-box chip) plus drop-out deactivation of ineffective heaters (~36.5% fewer iterations at 5 layers). [in situ + drop-out · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [36.5% · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)
- Multimodal preprocess: vision ([MNIST](../common/mnist.md)) → clip + FC features; audio (Spoken_numbers_pcm) → FFT sampling; touch → glove bend sensors—each to 16 optical intensities. [datasets · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

On-chip optical nonlinear activation is noted as missing here and proposed via future Ge/Si hybrid chips; that outlook is not the same as configuration-encoded structural nonlinearity discussed elsewhere in this Library. [nonlinear future · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

## Key results

Four-class classification on vision / audio / touch test sets: 86% / 82% / 89% (average 85.7%). [85.7% multimodal · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) Estimated potential 217.6 TOPS, 447.7 TOPS/mm², system-level 7.28 TOPS/W, optical latency ~30.2 ps (Table 1 comparison). [TOPS metrics · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [summary · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

These metrics address [scalable programmable photonic AI](../common/scalable-programmable-photonic-ai.md) from an integrated on-chip diffractive + in situ angle. The Library’s metasurface Perspective (paper-7362b59623cb46c3) frames a free-space programmable metasurface path; do not treat the two as interchangeable without further shared evidence.

## Limits

Proof-of-concept scale (16 inputs / 4 classes); thermo-optic heaters; linear optical core without on-chip nonlinearity; multimodal features still digitally preprocessed; throughput figures are estimation-based at a reference detection rate. [scale · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [no on-chip NL · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3) [100 GHz note · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50677-3)

# Large-scale photonic computing with nonlinear disordered media

**Preprint.** arXiv:2310.07690v1 [physics.optics] (11 Oct 2023). [arXiv header · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [title · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

## Problem and idea

[Photonic neural networks](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) already implement large linear transforms, but **large-scale optical nonlinear nodes** remain scarce: multiple scattering gives fixed random projection equivalent to a single linear layer, while many prior nonlinearities are incoherent or leave the optical domain. [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [linear scattering limit · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

This paper demonstrates a free-space nonlinear photonic system: a disordered polycrystalline lithium niobate (LN) nanocrystal slab combines multiple scattering with χ² **second-harmonic generation (SHG)**. Fundamental-harmonic (FH) and SH speckles supply linear vs nonlinear features; only a digital Tikhonov linear readout is trained—the optical weights stay fixed. [χ² LN slab · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [readout + scale · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [setup · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

The work sits in photonic / neuromorphic computing for machine learning under von Neumann energy pressure. [accelerator drive · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) Established routes in the Introduction include [photonic chips (PIC / MZI-style)](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md), free-space diffractive layers, and **optical random projection** through disordered media encoded with a [spatial light modulator (SLM)](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md). [hardware zoo + scattering · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) This paper’s route is **free-space SLM encoding + material χ² optical nonlinearity in a disordered LN slab**, not integrated MRR/MZI training and not the Library’s [structural (configuration-encoded) nonlinearity](../common/structural-nonlinearity.md). [χ² vs χ³ · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [SLM phase encoding · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) It addresses [scalable programmable photonic AI](../common/scalable-programmable-photonic-ai.md) from a **large fixed analog feature map** angle (up to 27,648 inputs / 3,500 nonlinear outputs), with programmability limited to the digital readout in this work. [27,648 / 3,500 · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

## Key method

- **[Nonlinear disordered-media photonic computing](../common/nonlinear-disordered-media-photonic-computing.md):** disordered LN slab; SH (400 nm) features from random quasi-phase-matching + scattering, modeled as a third-order scattering tensor / outer-product map; FH speckles are the linear random-projection baseline. [Figure 1 · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [SH model · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)
- **Encoding:** phase-only [SLM](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md) at 800 nm FH; cameras read FH and SH intensities; digital linear regression (Tikhonov). [SLM + dual cameras · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [Tikhonov readout · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)
- **Training stance:** optical core untrained (not in-situ / on-chip BP); Discussion only suggests future trainable blocks / forward–forward. [untrained optical part · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [future training outlook · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

## Key results

Across **14** image-classification, regression, and graph tasks, nonlinear SH features consistently beat linear FH / simulated random projection (gains depend on task). Examples: sign-language digits **85.96%** vs **74.82%** (3,500 features); ASL **83.51%** vs **78.53%**; CIFAR-10 **52.20%** vs **49.15%**; yacht hydrodynamics R² **0.987** vs **0.943**. [SLD · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [ASL · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [CIFAR-10 · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [yacht R² · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) Also tested on [MNIST](../common/mnist.md) / Fashion-MNIST with reported nonlinear gains (details in Supplementary Fig. 1). [MNIST mention · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [Supp. Fig. 1 · p. 17](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) Scale claim: up to **27,648** input and **3,500** nonlinear output nodes. [scale · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) Estimated optical ops ~**18.8 TFLOPS** at 40 fps for the SLD-sized nonlinear map (fixed matrix; not a programmable GPU substitute). [TFLOPS · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

Code/data: Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.8386366 (paper-declared). [data statement · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1)

## Limits

Table-top femtosecond pump hurts energy efficiency (CW SH outlook noted); optical weights are fixed/non-programmable; SNR ~14 dB and 8-bit quantization matter for regression; nonlinear path slightly less stable than linear. [energy / CW · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [fixed weights · p. 15](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [SNR · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) [stability · p. 16](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00644-1) Related Library hubs use different routes (PIC + in-situ BP, on-chip DONN, metasurface edge vision)—do not equate without shared experimental evidence.

# Integrated platforms and techniques for photonic neural networks

**Survey identity.** npj Nanophotonics Review (2025) 2:40. DOI 10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z. This page records *this survey’s* integrated-PNN taxonomy and synthesis; numerical claims about cited experiments are secondary (“as reported here”) unless the original paper is read separately. No datasets were generated in this review. [Review · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [DOI · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [data availability · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

## Research questions

1. How can [photonic neural networks (PNNs)](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) be built from integrated building blocks—linear operators, nonlinear operators, and fan-in/fan-out—on [photonic integrated circuits (PICs)](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md)? [neuron sequence + review scope · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)
2. Which on-chip device families (MZI meshes, MRR weight banks, non-volatile PCM memory, electro-optic modulators, on-chip diffractive metasurfaces / [DONNs](../common/on-chip-diffractive-optical-neural-network.md), MMI/3D waveguides) currently implement those blocks, and how do hybrid OE versus material all-optical nonlinear routes differ? [overview · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [nonlinear split · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)
3. What remains for multi-layer PIC cascades, end-to-end all-optical activation, and monolithic heterogeneous co-integration toward [scalable programmable photonic AI](../common/scalable-programmable-photonic-ai.md)? [multi-layer · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [all-optical NL · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [monolithic · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

Deep-learning compute pressure and transistor scaling limits motivate photonic accelerators. [deep learning / Moore limits · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [PNNs](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) use amplitude/phase and device transfer functions to implement NN operations; discrete off-chip optics exist, but this survey argues **integration** is the main path for scalability and practical environments. [PNN + integration · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) Its spine is the photonic neuron sequence fan-in → linear ops → nonlinear activation → fan-out on PICs—not free-space SLM stacks, fixed free-space metasurface cameras, or disordered-media χ² feature maps (those Library routes are complementary; this review does not equate them). [building blocks · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [PIC linear ops · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

## Taxonomy used in this survey

| Axis | Categories in this paper | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Neuron stages | Fan-in → linear operator → nonlinear operator → fan-out | Organizing spine |
| Linear-device families | MZI meshes; MRR weight banks; non-volatile PCM/memory; EO modulator arrays; on-chip diffractive metasurfaces ([DONN](../common/on-chip-diffractive-optical-neural-network.md)); MMI / 3D waveguides | How weights/transforms are realized |
| Nonlinear route | Active OE devices (PDs, lasers, modulators) vs material all-optical (PCM, 2D materials) | Expressivity vs OE conversion cost |
| I/O platform | Si EOMs vs TFLN; GeSi and other PDs (Table 1 synthesis) | Bandwidth, linearity, energy |
| System goal | Multi-layer PIC cascades; all-optical activation; monolithic heterogeneous PNNs | Outlook gaps |

These axes are **this Review’s framing**, not a universal hierarchy for other photonic surveys in the Library.

## Linear operators (device routes, as stated here)

**MZI meshes.** Reconfigurable unitary transforms; survey highlights coherent nanophotonic processors and complex-valued MZI chips (secondary citations). [MZI overview · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [representative demos · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

**MRR weight banks.** Broadcast-and-weight WDM weighting; feedback/feedforward control; in-situ gradient-descent weight control and tensor-convolution banks (as reported from cited works). [MRR / broadcast-and-weight · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [control + in-situ / tensor · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

**Non-volatile PCM / memory elements.** Retention without continuous power; spiking synapses, in-memory MAC cores, electronically reprogrammable PCM cells (survey synthesis). [non-volatile · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [PCM examples · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

**Electro-optical modulation.** Cascaded coherent modulators, SiGe crossbars, PIN attenuator arrays (including the Ashtiani et al. 2022 Nature image-classification chip cited as ref. 49—not the Library’s separate 2026 Ashtiani on-chip-BP hub). [modulator arrays · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [coherent / PIN demos · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [ref. 49 Ashtiani 2022 · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

**On-chip diffractive metasurfaces / DONNs.** Phase layers map fields; Fu et al. calibration on fixed 1D metasurfaces; Cheng et al. trainable multimodal DONN with in situ capability (Library hub [Cheng et al. 2024 TDONN](../paper-0b38aca306814214/index.md), cited here as ref. 56). [on-chip DONN · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [Fu + Cheng · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [ref. 56 · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

**Other.** MMI convolution units and 3D printed waveguides. [MMI / 3D · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

## Nonlinear operators and training notes

Survey synthesis: nonlinear stages use **active OE devices** (e.g., GeSi photodiodes, laser neurons) or **material all-optical** responses (PCM synapses, graphene/Si, MoTe₂ waveguide activators). [two families · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [active OE · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [all-optical motivation · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [PCM / 2D examples · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [In situ / physics-aware training](../common/physics-aware-training.md) appears in cited MRR control and monolithic coherent ONNs, but this review does not claim a new training algorithm. [in-situ MRR · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [monolithic in-situ training · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z)

## Fan-in / fan-out and on-chip systems

Fan-in emphasizes EOMs (Si plasma-dispersion limits vs TFLN Pockels linearity/bandwidth); Table 1 is this survey’s modulator comparison, not an original experiment. [fan-in / EOM · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [Si limits · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [TFLN + Table 1 · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) Fan-out focuses on PD bandwidth–responsivity trade-offs (GeSi examples). [fan-out · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) [GeSi PDs · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44310-025-00088-z) On-chip PNN exemplars (ACCEL, Taichi, coherent monolithic ONN) and Table 2 summarize reported power/speed/density from the literature. ## Outlook (survey synthesis)

Linear PIC operators are relatively mature (TOPS-class; some diffractive claims to POPS), but gaps remain: (a) cascaded multi-layer optical depth; (b) reconfigurable, low-power all-optical activations to escape hybrid OE bottlenecks (ADC/DAC, repeated O/E); (c) monolithic co-integration of fan-in/out, linear, and nonlinear elements via heterogeneous platforms (III–V, TFLN, Si/Si₃N₄, 2D). # Programmable metasurfaces for future photonic artificial intelligence

**Survey identity.** Nature Reviews Physics Perspective (also circulated as arXiv:2505.11659v1). This page records *this survey’s* taxonomy and synthesis; numerical claims about cited experiments are secondary (“as reported here”) unless the original paper is read separately. [arXiv header · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [publisher DOI · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

## Research questions

1. How can [photonic neural networks (PNNs)](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) become *scalable* enough that optical compute gains outweigh I/O overhead? [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)
2. Why do mature [photonic integrated circuits (PICs)](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md) and conventional free-space modulators struggle at billion-parameter scale, and can subwavelength [programmable optical metasurfaces](../common/programmable-optical-metasurface.md) close that gap? [PIC footprint · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [free-space → metasurface · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)
3. How should programmability enable [physics-aware / in situ training](../common/physics-aware-training.md) and [structural nonlinearities](../common/structural-nonlinearity.md) without relying solely on weak optical nonlinear materials? [Perspective scope · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [PAT needs reconfigurability · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

Digital AI energy demand is saturating conventional scaling; [PNNs](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) implement costly matrix–vector multiplies optically. [energy pressure · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [PNN idea · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Established hardware routes already include PICs, cavities, multimode fibre, and [spatial light modulators (SLMs)](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md), plus linear multilayer diffractive MVMs that lack reconfigurability. [hardware zoo · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) This Perspective argues that field-programmable metasurface hardware is the free-space route that can combine density with plasticity for the open problem of [scalable programmable photonic AI](../common/scalable-programmable-photonic-ai.md). [metasurface neural networks · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

## Taxonomy used in this survey

| Axis | Categories in this paper | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hardware geometry | 2D [PIC / MZI-style](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md) vs 3D free-space ([SLM](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md) vs subwavelength [metasurface](../common/programmable-optical-metasurface.md)) | Scalability & density |
| Programmability | Static diffractive layers vs electrically reconfigurable pixels | Continual learning / multitask |
| Training | In silico digital twins vs [physics-aware (PAT)](../common/physics-aware-training.md) / in situ updates | Simulation–reality gap |
| Nonlinearity | Material optical nonlinearity vs detector/intensity loops vs [structural nonlinearity](../common/structural-nonlinearity.md) | Deep-network expressivity |
| Modulation physics | Electro-optic, liquid crystal, phase-change, free-carrier, mechanical/chemical | Bandwidth, cyclability, CMOS fit |

These axes are **this Perspective’s framing**, not a universal hierarchy for other photonic surveys in the Library.

## Hardware routes and comparisons (as stated here)

**Integrated PIC path.** The survey reports that programmable PNNs have mostly used PICs, but 2D node footprints make billion-parameter chips unrealistic (example: scaling a 132-parameter on-chip network built with Mach–Zehnder modulators to ~3.4 m²). [MZI scaling example · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Wavelength multiplexing and 3D-printed interconnects are noted as partial mitigations that still leave reconfigurability/fabrication gaps. [alternatives · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

**Free-space SLM path.** Free-space setups avoid planar density limits but are described as bulky, slow, often reflection-only, and costly; LCoS SLMs additionally suffer strong inter-pixel fringing relative to liquid-crystal metasurfaces. [free-space limits · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [fringing vs metasurface · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Box 3 places LCoS SLMs beside PICs, GPUs, and *future* programmable metasurfaces as a metric comparison (survey synthesis, not a ranked benchmark). [Box 3 platforms · p. 21](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

**Programmable metasurface path (core proposal).** Reconfigurable/programmable metasurfaces (terms used interchangeably) are positioned as dense free-space modulators; a 300×300 nm² pixel argument yields ~0.9 cm² for 10⁹ parameters before packaging. [density claim · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Claimed PNN benefits include multitasking, structural nonlinearities, real-time/in situ learning, thinner stacks via higher NA, and fabrication-error robustness. [advantage list · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Modulation schemes reviewed: electro-optic (GHz-class), liquid-crystal (mature, slower unless subwavelength confined), phase-change, and slower free-carrier/mechanical/chemical options (Table I). [metrics · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [electro-optic · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [LC · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [PCM · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

**Early metasurface computing demos (secondary).** The survey states programmable metasurface *neural-network* demos remain scarce; an early 2021 GeSbTe waveguide mode-converter CNN is described as closer to the PIC paradigm with >10 µm² per operation. [scarce demos · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [2021 GeSbTe · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Image-processing metasurfaces with global (not pixel-wise) tuning are treated as related but distinct. [Green’s-function imagers · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

## Training and nonlinearity routes

**In silico vs physics-aware / in situ.** In silico training of a digital twin is simple but widens a simulation–reality gap with depth/steps. [in silico · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [PAT](../common/physics-aware-training.md) uses physical forward passes (backprop-in-the-loop or forward–forward) and, in the survey’s judgement, *requires* real-time reconfigurability—hence metasurface affinity and overlap with in situ learning. [PAT definition · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [PAT variants · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [reconfigurability requirement · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [real-time / in situ · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

**Physical nonlinear activation.** Purely linear multilayer diffractive MVMs collapse to one matrix and cannot capture XOR-like nonlinear maps (Box 4 pedagogical demo). [linear collapse · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [XOR · p. 22](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Material optical nonlinearities are weak; the survey’s distinctive route is [structural nonlinearity](../common/structural-nonlinearity.md): encode inputs in the programmable configuration *c* so the transfer operator H(*c*) supplies a nonlinear map through linear wave physics plus control circuitry. [challenge · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [definition · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [H(c) mechanism · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

## Open challenges (survey outlook)

CMOS foundry adaptation, via-hole / active-matrix pixel addressing down to subwavelength pitches, co-design of photonics+electronics, and new hybrid digital–optical software stacks remain barriers before commercial “field-programmable metasurface arrays (FPMA)”. [CMOS · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [addressing · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) [FPMA vision · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7) Optical computers are framed as special-purpose rather than general-purpose transistor replacements. [special-purpose · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-025-00831-7)

# Physical neural networks using sharpness-aware training

Nature Communications (2026) 17:1766. DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9. [DOI · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

## Problem and idea

[Physical / photonic neural networks (PNNs)](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) promise speed and energy efficiency, but training remains unreliable: **in silico** digital twins suffer model–reality gaps; **in situ** loops yield device-specific weights that transfer poorly across fabrication variance; both fail under post-deployment drift or misalignment and often need retraining. [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [in silico vs in situ · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

This paper proposes [sharpness-aware training (SAT)](../common/sharpness-aware-training.md): jointly seek a low loss *and* a flat (low-sharpness) region of the physical loss landscape so small parameter errors do not explode the loss. SAT applies in both in silico and in situ settings, enables cross-device transfer, and keeps accuracy under perturbations without retraining. [SAT benefits · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [flat minima · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

The work sits in neuromorphic / [photonic neural computing](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) under digital-hardware efficiency pressure. [neuromorphic PNNs · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) Training—not only inference—is the bottleneck: conventional BP is hard on physical hardware, and analog systems are disturbance-sensitive. [training lag · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) Established routes split into **in silico** (train a digital model, program hardware) vs **[in situ / physics-aware](../common/physics-aware-training.md)** (loop the device; PAT/DAT-style proxies). [two categories · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [PAT/DAT · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

Hardware demos span **integrated** [PIC](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md) platforms—thermally tuned **MRR weight banks** (experiment) and **MZI meshes** (simulation)—and **free-space** diffractive NNs using an OLED plus [SLM](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md) (experiment), including cases without an explicit misalignment→parameter model. [MRR / MZI / diffractive · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [unknown misalignment model · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) This is **not** the Library’s fixed MetaExtractor camera, programmable-metasurface Perspective, χ² disordered-media feature map, or Ashtiani et al. 2026 on-chip BP gradient hardware—those are complementary routes; do not rank them from this paper alone.

SAT addresses [scalable programmable photonic AI](../common/scalable-programmable-photonic-ai.md) from a **robust, transferable training-algorithm** angle across platforms and tasks (classification, compression, reconstruction, generation). [task breadth · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [Discussion summary · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

## Key method

- **Objective:** minimize task loss plus a sharpness / sensitivity penalty; practical update uses a first-order SAM-style two-step differentiation (α ≈ 0.1). [Eq. (2) goals · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [Eq. (3) · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [α ≈ 0.1 · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)
- **In silico SAT (MRR):** train on a deliberately inaccurate identical-MRR digital model (ignore crosstalk/noise), deploy to a 4×4 MRR bank; flatter Hessian (λ_max 1.2 vs 746.8 for BP). [inaccurate model · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [λ_max · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)
- **In situ SAT (MZI):** combine SAT with PAT-style in situ training; improves accuracy under fabrication error and enables **transfer** of trained phases to other error realizations. [in situ SAT 97.1% · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [transfer 95.2% · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)
- **Model-free / free-space SAT:** finite-difference gradient w.r.t. rotation/shift/scale for OLED–[SLM](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md) misalignment; train in silico assuming perfect alignment, test under affine errors. [finite difference · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [misalignment results · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)
- **Comparisons in this paper:** vs standard BP, noise-aware training (NAT), optical pruning, PAT, and DAT—conditions and metrics are paper-specific, not Library-wide rankings. [NAT / pruning · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [six MZI approaches · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

Physical nonlinearity: main experiments use linear optics + digital nonlinearity; a supplementary simulation with saturable absorber + PD quadratic NL is reported as compatible, not a structural-nonlinearity claim. [nonlinear simulation · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

## Key results

**MRR in silico (MNIST).** Ideal train ~99%; after deploy with model mismatch, SAT keeps **97.0%** vs BP **80.0%** at 22 °C; under 21–23 °C TEC sweep BP collapses (to ~17%) while SAT stays robust; without TEC at 20 °C, SAT **91.0%** vs BP **52.0%** (NAT/pruning ~73%). [97% vs 80% · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [91% no TEC · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [NAT/pruning · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

**MRR CIFAR-10.** Under −0.25 °C shift, ResNet18-style classification: SAT **83.4%** vs BP **10.6%**; autoencoder reconstruction MSE stays ~0.023 (SAT) vs collapse 0.529 (BP); GAN FID/images remain stable under SAT. [CIFAR classification/recon · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [generation · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

**MZI hybrid (simulation, MNIST).** Under σ_ps = σ_bs = 0.15: in silico SAT **92.3%**, in situ SAT **97.1%**, transfer accuracy **95.2%** vs DAT drop to **58.6%**; λ_max ≪ DAT. [in silico SAT · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [in situ SAT · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [transfer · p. 9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

**Free-space SLM (MNIST).** At 1° rotation: SAT **98.0%** vs BP **43.0%**; 1-pixel shift 97% vs 36%; scale 1.05 → 93% vs 12%. [misalignment accuracies · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

Code/data: GitHub `cuhkhuangslab/Sharpness-Aware-Training` and Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.17905440 (paper-declared). [code · p. 13](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [data · p. 13](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

## Limits

Extra automatic-differentiation cost vs single BP (mitigation via related “sharpness for free” ideas noted); MRR demos use a small weight bank and thermal control; MZI results are numerical; free-space train assumes ideal alignment then tests affine errors; main hardware path is linear with digital NL (nonlinear deep D2NN only in simulation). [training cost · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9) [nonlinear note · p. 12](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68470-9)

# Optical metasurfaces for general vision processing on the edge

Nature (2026). DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z. [DOI · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

## Problem and idea

Large vision foundation models demand cloud-scale compute, so latency- and energy-sensitive edge applications are hard to serve digitally. [edge pressure · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [Optical neural networks (ONNs)](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) promise parallelism and efficiency, but experimental systems often stay at ~10^5 parameters and simple tasks when forced to emulate digital algebra optically. [ONN limits · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

This paper embeds three computer-vision principles—similarity (RBF), attention-like aggregation, and local–global fusion—into a large free-space [optical metasurface](../common/optical-metasurface.md) (MetaExtractor) plus a co-designed 87,000-parameter digital back end, aiming at general-purpose edge vision rather than algebraic replicas of digital nets. [CV-physics paradigm · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [41M + 87k system · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

The work sits in photonic / optical neural computing for AI, targeting **edge computer vision** (detection, segmentation, 3D, video) under natural light. [ONN + edge vision · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) The hardware route is **free-space metasurface diffraction**, not an integrated [PIC / MZI / MRR](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md) mesh. [metasurface chip · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) Unlike the Library’s [programmable optical metasurface](../common/programmable-optical-metasurface.md) path, this MetaExtractor is **fixed after fabrication** and uses Gaussian-distributed meta-atoms to approximate RBF kernels so one chip serves many tasks without optical reconfiguration. [fixed metasurface · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [RBF / attention / local–global · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) A [spatial light modulator (SLM)](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md) appears only in the **lab** pipeline to synthesize dataset optical fields; the deployable prototype uses packaged metasurface cameras under ambient light. [lab SLM · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [natural-light prototype · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) Digital weights are trained; the optical layer is not in-situ trained. [digital-only training · p. 11](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

## Key method

- **MetaExtractor:** ~41 million meta-atoms on a ~10 mm² chip; free-space propagation at ~1 mm / ~6 mm extracts local / global features; sensor compresses 256 kernel channels. [41M atoms · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [distances · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)
- **Digital FusionNet + task heads:** 87k parameters fuse optical features and emit detection, segmentation, depth, and video outputs. [FusionNet · p. 4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)
- **Edge prototype:** two metasurface modules + Jetson Nano; field segmentation under natural scenes. [prototype · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [Jetson · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

## Key results

On [Cityscapes](../common/cityscapes.md), multitask feed-forward reports detection IOU **62.8%**, segmentation IOU **64.8%**, depth RMSE **0.91**, with large reported digital-parameter/energy reductions versus sequential SOTA models. [det 62.8% · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [seg 64.8% · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [RMSE 0.91 · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [efficiency · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) Campus prototype segmentation IOU **82.7%** at ~18.7 ms on Jetson Nano. [82.7% · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [18.7 ms · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

This addresses [scalable programmable photonic AI](../common/scalable-programmable-photonic-ai.md) from a **fixed free-space metasurface + tiny digital** angle. Related Library hubs: programmable-metasurface Perspective (`paper-7362b59623cb46c3`); on-chip trainable DONN (`paper-0b38aca306814214`)—do not equate routes without shared experimental evidence.

## Limits

Optical front end is non-reconfigurable after fab; lab evaluation uses SLM-generated fields and filtered LED before the natural-light prototype; many headline comparisons mix digital SOTA baselines with different pretraining; Si metasurface wavelength/transmission constraints require filtering or NIR bands. [no reconfig · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [lab SLM · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [pretraining note · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z) [NIR filter · p. 10](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10635-z)

# Integrated photonic neural network with on-chip backpropagation training

Nature (2026). DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8. [DOI · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [abstract · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)

## Problem and idea

[Photonic neural networks (PNNs)](../common/photonic-neural-network.md) need high-quality training, but scalable on-chip activation *gradients* have been missing, so prior work often runs backpropagation on a digital computer (fragile under device and environmental variation) or uses gradient-free alternatives. [training bottleneck · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [offline BP / alternatives · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)

This paper demonstrates an integrated silicon deep PNN trained **end-to-end with on-chip gradient-descent backpropagation**: linear weights and nonlinear ReLU activations *and* their gradients are realized with standard photonic components on one chip (controlled by off-chip electronics), matching a reference digital model at **>90%** accuracy on two nonlinear classification tasks while remaining robust to fabrication variation. [demonstration · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [on-chip BP claim · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)

## Concept route (for non-specialists)

The work sits in photonic / optical neural computing for AI, focusing on **how to train** integrated PNNs rather than only inference. [PNN motivation · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) The hardware route is a [photonic integrated circuit (PIC)](../common/photonic-integrated-circuit.md)—PIN attenuators for weights and ReLU, with MRM-based activation circuits also proposed—not free-space [SLM](../common/spatial-light-modulator.md) / [metasurface](../common/optical-metasurface.md) stacks. [Si foundry chip · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [PIN / MZI / MRM · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) Training follows [physics-aware / in situ](../common/physics-aware-training.md) on-chip BP so updates track the fabricated hardware, unlike digital-twin BP that ignores unmodeled variation. [robust vs digital train · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) Optoelectronic modulator nonlinearities here are **not** the Library’s [structural nonlinearity](../common/structural-nonlinearity.md) route (configuration-encoded maps). [optoelectronic ReLU · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) This addresses [scalable programmable photonic AI](../common/scalable-programmable-photonic-ai.md) from an integrated on-chip BP angle; related hubs include TDONN in situ training (`paper-0b38aca306814214`) and free-space metasurface edge vision (`paper-d89dab569d0d4dc4`)—do not equate routes without shared experimental evidence.

## Key method

- **Chip:** input → hidden (8 neurons) → output; forward path for inference and separate backward path for layer errors δ; AMF SOI fabrication. [architecture · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [AMF process · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)
- **Nonlinearity:** PIN attenuator ReLU + gain-switched gradient (proof of concept); sigmoid/ReLU circuits also shown with intensity modulators and MRMs. [sigmoid/MRM · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [ReLU · p. 2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)
- **Training:** on-chip BP (η = 0.05); microcontroller stores data and applies final ReLU/MSE in the reported setup. [training loop · p. 7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)

## Key results

XOR classification after on-chip BP; 2D point-separation with **92.5%** peak inference accuracy; five-trial robustness shows on-chip train+infer matches TensorFlow reference and beats digital-train then on-chip-infer under device variation. [XOR + 92.5% · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [robustness · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) Abstract reports **over 90%** accuracy matching the digital reference without using a digital computer for BP. [>90% · p. 1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)

## Limits

Proof-of-concept scale (2 inputs, one hidden layer); separate forward/backward paths increase optics and area (hardware-reuse and WDM proposed); final output ReLU and cost partly in microcontroller; no photonic memory; total system power ~4.34 W train / ~3.69 W infer in the reported board setup. [scaling limits · p. 5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [microcontroller · p. 3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [power · p. 8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8) [memory · p. 6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10262-8)
